Questions, answered.

What is proactive intelligence?

Proactive intelligence is AI that notices what needs attention, connects it to your goals, plans the next useful step, and carries approved work forward with human oversight and a record of its actions.

How is it different from a chatbot?

A chatbot usually responds to a request. Proactive intelligence also assesses relevant changes against existing goals, chooses a justified next step and maintains continuity. It should ask for essential decisions and respect the authority already granted.

Is it the same as an automated workflow?

A workflow follows a defined sequence. Proactive intelligence adds contextual judgment about whether a change matters and which next step is useful. Defined workflows and deterministic approval checks can still carry out parts of that work.

Does proactive mean acting without permission?

No. Initiative does not grant authority. A signal can request assessment without authorizing an external action. Work remains subject to the permissions, approvals and connections enabled for the company.

What does SINGULANCE build?

SINGULANCE is building proactive intelligence: company memory, an AI Chief of Staff and specialist AI teammates that help carry work forward. HIVEMIND provides company context, Runtime coordinates work, HyperAgents perform specialist assignments, and ICARUS explores agent memory.

Is every capability available to every account?

No. SINGULANCE is in early access. Availability depends on account access, configured connections and permissions. The operating cycle on this page describes the design direction, not a guarantee that every scenario is production-verified.

ICARUS — the memory filesystem for AI agents

October 19, 2026  ·  By SINGULANCE Labs

Back to Research
Share the post

Highlights

  • Durable local memory with lexical recall, without an account or API key.
  • A self-contained CLI for macOS, Linux and Windows.
  • Memory tools for Codex, Claude Code and Cursor; Harness stays opt-in.
  • Optional developer email/Google sign-in, separate from company workspaces.
IC
ICARUS
.amr format

A memory filesystem for AI agents — one mmap’d file per tenant, no server.

Start here · CLI v0.3.91

Local memory. Ready for your agent.

One self-contained binary. No Node.js or Rust required on macOS Apple Silicon/Intel, Linux x64/ARM64, or Windows x64. Local memory works without an account or API key.

1. Install

macOS / Linux / WSL

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amar3012005/ICARUS/main/install.sh | bash

Native Windows PowerShell

irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amar3012005/ICARUS/main/install.ps1 | iex

Choose Agent Memory for the default local experience. Knowledge Space is a preview; Harness is an explicit opt-in. On Windows, run icarus setup after installation for guided setup.

Open a new terminal after installation. To use the current macOS/Linux terminal:

export PATH="$HOME/.icarus/bin:$PATH"
icarus --version

2. Save and recall

icarus save "The release checklist lives in docs/release.md" --org first-memory
icarus recall "release checklist" --org first-memory

3. Connect your coding agent — optional

From the repository root, choose codex, claude, or cursor. This registers memory tools and creates the repository memory shard. Restart the coding agent after registration.

icarus mcp install codex
# Add --harness only when this repository should use task governance.

4. Developer sign-in — optional

icarus connect

Choose email or Google on the ICARUS developer account page. For email, enter the six-digit code from your ICARUS email and choose Verify and continue. The browser returns to the waiting terminal, which confirms sign-in.

Keep the terminal open; it waits up to fifteen minutes. If it expires after the browser verified you, run icarus connect again to finish using that session. No purchase or company workspace is required. Developer identity grants no hosted customer API access and does not upload local memory.

Skip sign-in to keep working offline. Use icarus connect --logout to remove the local developer credential. Upgrade later with icarus update.

Read the quickstartDownloads and checksumsDeveloper sign-in details

Agent Bus is experimental with no public installer; the proposed bridge is not shipped. Computer Use is a separate experimental module. Installing Memory enables neither.

v1 made a claim; v2 ships the system. Since June, ICARUS went from a frozen format RFC to a production Rust engine behind HIVEMIND: seven machine-verified gates, a live cutover serving real tenants, and — new in v2 — every memory it builds is post-quantum signed by default. This revision documents what was actually built, with the numbers each gate had to pass.

From thesis to production — seven gates

Nothing advanced on judgment. Each phase ended in a gate: a scripted, reproducible pass/fail check on real data — real bge-m3 embeddings of real production memories, never synthetic vectors. A phase that failed its gate could not advance.

the build — seven gates, each machine-verifiedclick a gate
P6 — Node binding + cutoverrecall parity 1.00

napi addon + MnemeVectorStore — a drop-in for the Qdrant client. Eval gate: recall@5 parity 1.00 vs the live stack on real data. Soak testing surfaced and fixed a real concurrent-reserve segfault (RwLock write-guard).

The engine that emerged: a Rust core (.mseg slots + usearch HNSW overlay + PQ codebooks), write-path isolated from indexing, exposed to Node through a napi binding whose store class is a drop-in for the vector-DB client it replaces. Soak testing under concurrent load surfaced a real segfault in incremental indexing — found, root-caused to an unguarded reserve, fixed with a write-guard, and regression-tested. That is what the gates are for.

The .amr slot — unchanged, and that’s the point

The 202-byte slot frozen in the v1 RFC survived production contact without a single field change. The format is the contract:

.amr slot — 202 byteshover a field
046142234162170
vector_pqoffset 34 · 128 B

1024-dim embedding → 128 bytes via Product Quantization. 32× compression. The vector IS in the slot, not a foreign key.

How it runs live — anchor + engine

In production, ICARUS does not replace the relational layer — memory is a relational hub (provenance, projects, embeddings all reference it). The deployed topology keeps a thin relational anchor per memory and moves the hot path — semantic + entity + temporal + graph recall — onto the .amr engine. One file per tenant, opened in-process by the memory engine, with the recall backend live-verified against the previous stack before cutover (recall-parity gate: 1.00).

LayerRole in the live system
Relational anchorOne row per memory — identity, provenance, project links. The FK hub stays.
.amr shard (per tenant)The recall engine: PQ vectors, entity bitmaps, bi-temporal anchors, adjacency — one mmap.
HNSW overlayAsync-built index; writes never wait for indexing (p99 54.75 µs under rebuild).

Abstract

Artificial intelligence systems today are overwhelmingly model-centric. Intelligence is assumed to live inside a model or an agent, while memory, tools, and workflows remain auxiliary attachments.

At SINGULANCE Labs, we propose Cognitive Swarm Intelligence (CSI): an environment-centric architecture in which intelligence is not treated as a property of any single agent, but as an emergent property of a shared, persistent, structured cognitive environment.

CSI combines structured memory, stigmergic coordination, adaptive routing, procedural consolidation, agent identity, and a controlled meta-loop into a single architecture. The result is a system designed not merely to answer questions, but to remember, coordinate, execute, improve, and accumulate operational intelligence over time.

[01] The problem — why agent-centric AI has structural limits

LimitWhy it bites
Transient knowledgeEven when external memory exists, it is treated as static retrieval context rather than an active medium for cognition.
Brittle coordinationMulti-agent systems coordinate through explicit communication — costly, brittle, and hard to scale.
No procedural learningRepeated successes do not harden into reusable behavior. Every session starts from scratch.
Lost reasoningSystems store outputs but not the pathways that produced them — decision rationale is lost.

[02] Core thesis — the central claim

“Persistent shared cognition can outperform isolated agent reasoning when memory, behavior, and policy are all externalized into a structured environment.”

#ClaimWhat it means
1Intelligence can be externalizedStore competence in the environment — decisions, facts, execution trails, blueprints, confidence signals — not only in weights or prompt history.
2Coordination emerges without heavy messagingAgents cooperate through shared state — trails, observations, graph relationships — not explicit communication.
3Learning occurs without retrainingThe system improves by changing structure: successful paths strengthen, repeated sequences become blueprints, weak paths decay, routing adapts.
4Identity stays local, intelligence stays globalAgents differ by role, skill, and reputation, but competence is shared — agents are access points into a common substrate.
5Self-improvement requires control, not chaosA bounded meta-loop: observe, evaluate, recommend, apply — through a controlled parameter registry with rollback.

[03] Architecture — a three-layer cognitive runtime

LayerNamespaceRole
Canonical Knowledgekg/*Durable, validated knowledge — entities, relationships, procedures, decisions. The long-lived source of truth.
Operational Cognitionop/*The active life of the system — goals, trails, execution events, observations, attempts, decision candidates.
Control & Learningmeta/*Evaluative signals — reputation, trail weights, decay schedules, blueprint thresholds, routing parameters. The control plane.

[04] Key concepts — how CSI works

Five interconnected mechanisms let intelligence emerge from the environment rather than reside in any single agent.

Trails — behavior as first-class structure. A trail is a compact, structured representation of how progress toward a goal can be made. Unlike raw logs, trails are directly actionable — connecting goal context to next steps, shaped by success, failure, cost, latency, conflict, congestion, and reputation. “Given this context and this goal, what path has proven useful?”

Blueprints — from repetition to procedure. When the system detects repeated successful patterns across execution traces, it promotes them into reusable composite trails — its emerging habits. This is how the system learns how to act, not merely remember what happened.

Force-Based Routing — cognitive physics for action selection. Instead of hard-coded path selection, the system computes a force profile over candidate trails, combined via softmax to preserve exploration while exploiting strong pathways. Toggle the forces to feel how the swarm chooses:

Agent Identity — without agent-centric intelligence. Each agent has an identity, role, declared skills, observed competence, reputation, and specialization confidence — yet intelligence remains shared. “Agents have roles. The environment has memory. Intelligence emerges from their interaction.”

The Meta-Loop — safe self-improvement. A bounded three-part loop turns self-improvement from uncontrolled self-editing into policy evolution through configuration: a read-only Dashboard (success rates, blueprint usage, force contributions), a batch MetaEvaluator (detects patterns, produces recommendations), and an auditable Parameter Registry with rollback.

Not…Because
Not just RAGRAG retrieves text. CSI stores structured outcomes, execution traces, and reusable behavior. Retrieval is one component.
Not just a memory systemMemory preserves data. CSI preserves data and behavior — turning repeated success into procedures and shaping future policy.
Not just orchestrationOrchestrators move tasks. CSI evolves how those paths are chosen and reused over time.

OutcomeWhat changes
Competence survives replacementReplacing the agent does not destroy intelligence — it has been externalized into the environment.
Operational intelligence accumulatesOrganizations build compound knowledge rather than losing it when sessions end or teams change.
Improvement without retrainingSystems improve through usage by evolving policies, procedures, and routing — not model weights.
Auditable reasoningReasoning becomes persistent and traceable through structured trails and decision provenance.
Structural coordinationCoordination emerges through shared-environment modifications rather than expensive message overhead.
Policy evolutionLearning by evolving policies and procedures instead of re-running costly reasoning loops.

Sovereign memory engine

The memory layer that remembers everything your org knows — now quantum-resistant end to end: transport, integrity, and audit.

Why — the threat model

An adversary who can't break today's crypto can still record encrypted traffic now and decrypt it later, once a cryptographically-relevant quantum computer exists ("harvest-now, decrypt-later"). Separately, an attacker with DB access could try to forge or silently rewrite stored memories or audit logs. HIVEMIND addresses both with quantum-resistant primitives at the transport, data-integrity, and audit layers.

The three layers at a glance

LayerPurposePrimitiveStandard

ML-KEM sealed

Layer 1 — Hybrid post-quantum TLS

Every connection to HIVEMIND is negotiated with a hybrid key exchange — two independent secrets, combined:

hybrid key exchange
shared_secret = combine(
    classical_ECDH,        // fast, proven today
    lattice_KEM            // quantum-hard (FIPS 203)
)

The session key is safe unless both the classical and the lattice problem are broken at once — so it is never weaker than today's crypto, and quantum-resistant on top. The practical consequence: an adversary who records the encrypted stream today cannot decrypt it later, even with a future quantum computer. Older clients that don't understand the hybrid negotiation fall back to the classical curve, so nothing breaks.

Layer 2 — Memory write integrity

Every time a memory is written, HIVEMIND signs a canonical, deterministic representation of the record — the exact same bytes can be reconstructed later:

payload   = canonical({ id, user, org, content })   // keys sorted, stable
signature = sign(payload, private_key)               // lattice signature

The signature is stored alongside the memory, not inside it, and the signing key lives only in the environment — never in the database. So an attacker who reaches the database and rewrites content cannot produce a matching signature: forgery needs the secret key, and the secret key isn't there to steal. Anyone holding only the public key can verify the memory is authentic and unaltered.

Layer 3 — Tamper-evident audit chain

Security-relevant events are chained like a mini-ledger: each entry commits to the one before it, then the commitment is signed.

entry_hash = hash( previous_entry_hash + canonical(entry) )
signature  = sign(entry_hash, audit_private_key)     // hash-based signature

Because every entry's hash folds in the previous entry's hash, the log is append-only: you can't insert, delete, or reorder a single event without breaking every link after it. The first entry anchors the chain (no predecessor). The signatures use a hash-based scheme — the most conservative post-quantum family, resting on the fewest assumptions — because an audit trail is exactly where you want maximum paranoia. A periodic checkpoint signs the head of the chain, so the entire history can be verified in one shot.

The whole model rests on one principle: the secret keys never live where the data lives. Signing keys exist only in the runtime environment; the database holds signatures and public keys, nothing that could forge them. Compromising the database therefore does not grant the ability to forge a memory or rewrite the audit log — the attacker would still be missing the one thing that matters.

Verification is public by design: anyone with the public key can independently confirm authenticity, without any privileged access. And every layer degrades gracefully — if a signing key is absent, the write still succeeds, just unsigned. Availability is never sacrificed for signing; integrity is added on top, never in the critical path.

Overall accuracy on LongMemEval — the industry-standard benchmark for long-context conversational memory. Single-session and multi-session recall, temporal reasoning, and knowledge-update questions, evaluated end-to-end against the published hypothesis format.

What LongMemEval actually tests

LongMemEval is the benchmark long-context memory systems get judged against — not a synthetic retrieval toy, but multi-session conversational histories with single-session questions, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning across sessions, and knowledge-update questions where an earlier fact is later corrected. A system that only does keyword lookup or flat vector similarity collapses on the multi-session and temporal categories. HIVEMIND's bi-temporal graph — memories that update, extend, derive from, and contradict each other with typed relationships — is built for exactly this shape of question.

Published methodology

LongMemEval question set + evaluation harness are public. Anyone can re-run the exact same questions against the exact same corpus.

No cherry-picked runs

The reported score is the full-set average, not a best-of-N run. Regressions below the pass/fail gate block deploys.

Live regression gate

Every recall-path change re-runs the retrieval benchmark (P@5 / R@10 / NDCG@10 / MRR) before shipping — a regression fails the gate, not the customer.

Reproducible on your data

The same Evaluation surface ships inside every HIVEMIND workspace — run the benchmark against your own memories, not just ours.

HIVEMIND vs. the alternatives

Keyword search fails the moment a question is phrased differently from the source text. Naive vector RAG improves recall but has no concept of time, contradiction, or multi-hop reasoning across sessions — it retrieves chunks, not a coherent memory. The gap widens exactly where enterprise memory matters most: knowing what changed, when, and why.

- A scope grant limited to what the connected feature actually uses
- Your ability to disconnect and revoke access at any time from the Connectors page

Data accessed through a connected service is processed only for the purpose you authorized (ingestion, recall, or an action you requested) and is subject to that service’s own terms as well.

## AI Processing

When you use HIVEMIND’s recall, chat, or agent features, your content may be processed by model providers routed through our controlled AI gateway solely to generate the response or action you requested. We do not permit these providers to train on your data. Where a connector routes execution through a third-party platform (for example, Composio for certain tool integrations), the same principle applies — processing happens at your direction, for your request, and nothing else.

## Use of Information

- Operating and authenticating your account
- Storing, indexing, and recalling memory as you request it
- Executing connector actions you explicitly authorize
- Billing, plan enforcement, and fraud prevention
- Essential service communications
- Security monitoring and abuse prevention
- Compliance with legal obligations under GDPR, DORA, and applicable law

## Data Residency & Hosting

Hosted HIVEMIND workspaces apply organization and user scope across application, database, vector-search, and graph paths. Dedicated and self-hosted deployment options provide additional physical isolation where contracted. Primary application and memory infrastructure is operated in Europe; a connector or model provider you deliberately invoke may process the minimum necessary request outside the EEA under an applicable transfer mechanism described below.

## Service Providers & Sub-processors

Depending on the product and configuration you use, service providers may include:

- Cloudflare for DNS, edge delivery, security controls, Workers, and controlled AI routing
- EU infrastructure providers, including Hetzner, for application, database, and memory services
- PostHog EU Cloud for optional aggregate product analytics only after consent; session replay is disabled
- Stripe for checkout, subscriptions, and payment records; SINGULANCE does not store full card numbers
- Google or other identity providers when you choose their sign-in method
- Model and connector providers needed for a feature you request, subject to the selected deployment and routing configuration

We review this list when providers or processing purposes change and update this notice before materially different optional processing is enabled.

## Information Disclosure

We do not sell, rent, or commercially trade your personal information. We disclose information only:

- To infrastructure and processing subprocessors necessary to run the Services (see Infrastructure Partners)
- To third-party AI providers, solely to fulfil a request you made
- To services you explicitly connected, per the scope you authorized
- When required by law, regulation, or valid legal process
- To protect the rights, safety, or property of SINGULANCE, our users, or others
- In connection with a merger, acquisition, or asset transfer, with continuity of this policy

## Data Retention & Deletion

We retain account and memory data for as long as your account is active, or as needed to provide the Services, subject to configured retention and legal obligations. Consent records are retained for the stated cookie lifetime, optional analytics identifiers for the period listed in the Cookie Policy, and payment or tax records for applicable statutory periods. You may delete individual memories, disconnect a connector, or request full account deletion at any time. Disconnecting a service stops new sync but does not automatically delete previously ingested data unless you request it. Full-account deletion requests are honored subject to legal retention requirements and reasonable processing time.

## Your Rights (GDPR)

As a data subject under GDPR (and equivalent rights under other applicable law), you may:

- Request access to the personal data we hold about you
- Request correction of inaccurate data
- Request erasure of your data (“right to be forgotten”)
- Request restriction of, or object to, certain processing
- Request data portability in a structured, commonly-used format
- Withdraw consent for a connected service at any time
- Lodge a complaint with your local data protection authority

To exercise any of these rights, contact us — see Contact below.

We normally respond within one month after verifying the request. You may also complain to your competent supervisory authority, including the State Commissioner for Data Protection of Lower Saxony where applicable.

## International Transfers

Where a connected service or AI provider you authorize is based outside the EU/EEA, we rely on that provider’s Standard Contractual Clauses or equivalent safeguard, and only transfer the minimum data necessary to fulfil the request you made.

## Policy Updates

We may update this policy as our Services evolve. Material changes are communicated by email to account holders or a prominent notice in the product before they take effect.
